name: Blue cheatline (as worn in 1985)
description: Pan Am's scheme of the 1970s as most of its 727s and 747s still wore it in 1985: a gloss white body with a blue cheatline through the cabin windows from just behind the nose to the tail cone (the cockpit windows in it), a light grey lower fuselage under a level line a little below the windows, and a small black nose tip. 'PAN AM' in black extended capitals above the forward windows. The white fin carries the big blue globe, with 'PAN AM' across its middle. Bare metal engines. Each aircraft's 'Clipper' name was lettered small in script under the forward windows (not drawn).

titles.style: Black extended capitals of even weight above the forward cabin windows, aft of the forward door.

logos.description: The globe: a blue disc drawn with white lines of latitude and longitude, the name 'PAN AM' in white capitals across a band through its middle. Painted big on the fin, a little aft of the middle; on the 727 it reaches down over the centre engine's intake fairing.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on 727-235 N4740 (1984, fitted to shapes/B722.json), with the 747 as a type (B744-passenger stands in for the 747-100 and -200). Edges are fitted, not traced: the cheatline's edges are level lines at +1.08 m and +0.52 m (the windows run +0.6 to +1.0 m) and the grey's top a level line at -0.22 m, easing down only in front of the cockpit to the band's square tip at 1.1 m. Pan Am began repainting into the 'billboard' scheme (billboard) in 1984, so in 1985 both were flying; the A300s were delivered in the billboard and never wore this one. Colors are from faded slides: the blue is a mid blue, not the teal some photos show. The 727's globe and US flag, low on the fin and on the S-duct intake fairing, are in the B722 entry (types), so a type without its own entry gets the globe centered on its fin. Refitted 2026-11-24 on the passenger 727 (shapes/B722-passenger.json): on N4740, scaled by its doors, the cheatline runs 1.24-1.86 m under the crown with the windows in its middle and the grey's line 2.31 m under it; the band was 0.3 m high, now lowered, every edge level on the cabin. The title's baseline 1.07 m under the crown, its capitals 0.52 m. Added 2026-11-25: the 747SP (B74S) and L-1011-500 (L101-500) entries, each measured on its own shape from left-side photos of 1984-86. The SPs' band is the windows' own height (0.57 m) with the grey 1.1 m under the windows' middle; the -500s' band is about 0.7 m round the windows. Every edge is a level line in meters with a point at each crown and belly point of the shape, held within 0.3 mm of level between them. Re-measured 2026-11-25 on side-on photos of N750PA (1983) and N728PA (1984): the 747 entry's band is about 0.6 m round the windows (it had been 1 m, read off a three-quarter view), the grey 1.06 m under the windows' middle, the title 8.9 m by 0.9 m from door 1 (length over height about 10, it had been 12.6), the globe 5 m across. Added 2026-11-25: the 737-200 (B733 entry, on the 737-300 shape), measured on N70724 from both sides (1985 and 1986): a narrower band than the 727's, 0.62 m round the windows, the grey 0.55 m under the centerline with its front edge swept down to the belly behind the nose cone, a smaller globe and the flag high on the fin.

B722.note: On the 727 the globe is about 2.9 m across and centered at the top of the centre engine's S-duct intake, its lower half on the intake fairing, and the US flag is on that fairing ahead of the fin (N550PS, N4740). Both are in the fin's space carried down below its root, where a renderer draws fin logos over an S-duct's fairing. On other types the scheme's own globe is centered on the fin and the flag is left out.

titles.style: Black extended capitals of even weight above the forward cabin windows, aft of the forward door.

logos.description: The globe: a blue disc drawn with white lines of latitude and longitude, the name 'PAN AM' in white capitals across a band through its middle. Painted big on the fin, a little aft of the middle; on the 727 it reaches down over the centre engine's intake fairing.

The flag of the United States, about 1.9 times as wide as it is tall, the canton forward on both sides. On the 727 it's on the side of the centre engine's S-duct intake fairing, ahead of the fin and the registration, about 0.6 m tall: in the fin's space carried down, ahead of and below its root.

B733.note: Pan Am's 737-200s (the Internal German Service out of Berlin Tegel) wore the cheatline narrower than the 727's: a band about 0.62 m tall round the cabin windows (0.10-0.72 m above the centerline, the windows 0.25-0.59 m), its lower edge easing up in front of the cockpit to a point on the nose's crown about 0.9 m back, with white under it down to the grey's level line 0.55 m under the centerline. The grey's front edge sweeps down to the belly about 1.05 m back, behind the white nose cone and its small black tip. 'PAN AM' runs from just behind door 1 (6.2-11.9 m back), its capitals 0.52 m tall on a baseline 0.96 m up, 1.05 m under the crown as on the 727. The globe is about 2.6 m across a little aft of the fin's middle, the flag high near the leading edge, and the tailplane is grey like the wings. Measured on N70724 (left side, Tegel, March 1986, and right side, Zurich, May 1985) and checked on N385PA (1986) and N70723 (May 1984). The 737-300 shape stands in for the -200: the nose, the cabin's section and the tail are the same, so every edge is placed in meters from the nose or the tail; the -300 is 2.6 m longer in the cabin.

titles.style: Black extended capitals of even weight above the forward cabin windows, from just behind the forward door to a few windows short of the overwing exits.

logos.description: The globe: a blue disc drawn with white lines of latitude and longitude, the name 'PAN AM' in white capitals across a band through its middle. Painted big on the fin, a little aft of the middle; on the 727 it reaches down over the centre engine's intake fairing.
The flag of the United States, about 1.9 times as wide as it is tall, the canton forward on both sides. On the 737-200 it's high on the fin near its leading edge, above the globe, about 0.65 m tall.

B742.note: The 747's cheatline is about 0.6 m tall, round the main deck's windows with their middles in its middle, with white under it down to the grey 1.06 m under the windows' middle. It ends square about 0.9 m back from the nose, behind a white nose cone with a black tip, and runs aft until the belly's sweep up to the tail takes it. 'PAN AM' in black, about 0.9 m tall and 8.9 m long, sits under the hump from door 1 to just short of door 2. The globe is about 5 m across, a little aft of the fin's middle, the flag high above it. Measured side-on on N750PA (747-121, November 1983) and N728PA (747-212B, June 1984), left side; re-measured 2026-11-25 (the band had been 1 m tall and the grey 0.8 m under the side's middle, read off N726PA's three-quarter view). On the 747-100/-200 shape (shapes/B742.json) since 2026-11-25: its main deck is the 747-400's, and the title sits under the upper deck's three windows as on N750PA.

The flag of the United States, about 1.9 times as wide as it is tall, the canton forward on both sides. On the 747 it's high on the fin above the globe, about 1.1 m tall.

B74S.note: The 747SP's cheatline is the other 747s': a band about 0.57 m tall round the main deck's windows, with white under it down to the grey 1.1 m under the windows' middle. It ends square about 1.1 m back from the nose, behind the white nose cone with its black tip, and runs aft until the belly's sweep up to the tail takes it. 'PAN AM' sits under the upper deck's windows from just ahead of door 1 to just past door 2, about 0.9 m tall. The globe is about 4.9 m across in the fin's middle and the flag high above it. Measured on N532PA (July 1985) and N540PA (January 1986), both left side.
